clue.text: Actors were first to have moved two pieces at once

definitions.text: have moved two pieces at once

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast
to be first, at the front, is to have led

explanation.surface: A remark about which actors went first after moving some props around.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess, castling is the one move that shifts two pieces, king and rook, at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling in chess moves king and rook together, the only move of two pieces at a time.

clue.text: Mr Redgrave hasn't finished the port

parts.note: Corin Redgrave was an English actor of the Redgrave family

indicators.note: the word the loses its final letter, so it is not finished

explanation.surface: An actor named Redgrave has not finished drinking his port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink, but it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth is a Greek seaport on the isthmus between the Gulf of Corinth and the Saronic Gulf.

clue.text: Not quite the wrong thing for 9 13 in the 21

definitions.text: Not quite the wrong thing for 9 13 in the 21

parts.words: Not quite the wrong thing for 9 13 in the 21
parts.note: a square peg is the proverbial wrong thing for round holes; change one letter, so not quite that, and you get a fielding position in cricket

explanation.surface: A misfit is not quite right for a set of round holes out in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 and 13 give ROUND HOLES, recalling the square peg in a round hole; swap P for L and you have the cricket fielding position.
explanation.definitionFit: Square leg is a cricket fielding position level with the batsman on the leg side.

indicators.note: to sport with something is to play about with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone languishes, reading a tabloid newspaper, the Daily Sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Sport is a British tabloid. Languish is the surname of the heroine of Sheridan's play The Rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia Languish is the romantic heroine of Sheridan's comedy The Rivals, so her first name pairs with that surname.

indicators.note: the letters are played around with, giving a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 21 across, the cricket field

explanation.surface: A clever fielder pulled off a crafty trick on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceitful and false are synonyms: both describe someone who misleads or lies.

parts.note: obtained means got
OP is short for opus, a work
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: The founder of a firm got hold of some published works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' looks like a person who sets something up; here it is the verb meaning to collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: To founder is to fail or fall apart, which the idiom for going to ruin expresses.

definitions.meaning: a narrow ravine or water channel
a cricket fielding position between point and slips

explanation.surface: A channel runs across the playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A gully is both a small ravine cut by water and a fielding position in cricket.

parts.note: a trial is a test
a marriage is a match

explanation.surface: A couple try out a trial marriage on the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: A test match is an international cricket match, played on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is a game between national sides, something that takes place out on the cricket field.

definitions.meaning: ... is the everyday short name of ... Cymru, the Welsh nationalist party
a length of tartan cloth worn over the shoulder in Highland dress

explanation.surface: A Welsh element appears in a Scotsman's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the Welsh party (Welsh for party) and the tartan shoulder cloth of Highland costume.

clue.text: Adopted and raised a little boy among sheep

indicators.note: the boy and the a sit among the letters of the sheep

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep
Ken is a boy's name, a shortened form of Kenneth

explanation.surface: A small boy was adopted and brought up among a flock of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken up means both adopted, as of an idea, and lifted or raised.

definitions.meaning: a catch is a song sung in canon by several voices
a ball is spherical in shape

explanation.surface: A cricketer is told to take a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is a song for voices entering in turn, like a catch, and also describes a ball's shape.

clue.text: Lands awkwardly, interrupting chicken sandwich, perhaps

indicators.note: the mixed letters break into the middle of the bird

parts.note: a cock is a male chicken

indicators.note: the letters land awkwardly, out of order

explanation.surface: A chicken lands clumsily on someone's sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lands' looks like the verb for the chicken alighting, but it is just the letters to mix; 'interrupting' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich is an example of food eaten cold between meals.

clue.text: No weirdness in weird Tony Blair having upgraded his degree?

indicators.note: weird letters are strange and disordered, so they are rearranged
a BA upgraded to an MA swaps the B for M

explanation.surface: Tony Blair is weird for upgrading his university degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having upgraded his degree' changes the B of Blair to M (BA to MA), giving TONYMLAIR, which 'weird' then rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Normality is the state of being ordinary, the absence of anything strange.

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, its 1 read as I
the Don is a river in Yorkshire and in Russia

explanation.surface: A road and a river lie inside the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-on is a cricket fielding position near the bowler on the leg side.

definitions.meaning: a golf course is divided into these, eighteen of them

explanation.surface: Openings, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Holes are gaps, and a golf course consists of holes.

clue.text: The way with business is not to waver

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
with means and
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: Advice that a company's path is never to falter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand firm means to keep one's position resolutely and refuse to waver.

parts.note: original means first
a slip is a lapse or sin

explanation.surface: Adam's original sin committed in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original sin' suggests Eden, but each word gives a piece of a cricket position.
explanation.definitionFit: First slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper.

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
Mull is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides
ET is the alien of the film

explanation.surface: A revolutionary on an island meets an alien fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The red mullet is a Mediterranean food fish.

clue.text: Ridiculous to give Bella a hug?

indicators.note: letters that give, yield or bend, shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is it absurd to give a girl named Bella a cuddle?
explanation.definitionFit: Laughable and ridiculous are synonyms: both describe something worthy of mockery.

clue.text: A number in crooked dealings indicated (by the umpire?)

indicators.note: the number goes inside the mixed letters
crooked dealings are bent, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An umpire signals a number of crooked dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' turns DEALINGS into SIGNALED, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To signal is to indicate, as an umpire does with a raised arm or finger.

clue.text: Journeys of fliers when climbing on islands

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing reads the pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is made of fliers
as means when

explanation.surface: Airmen take journeys when climbing on island peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Safaris are expeditions or journeys, especially to watch wildlife in Africa.

definitions.meaning: a ... takes part in field sports such as hunting

explanation.surface: A sportsman is picked on in a field game.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound is to harass, and hounds are the dogs that take part in hunting.

parts.note: de is French for of
the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: Something lower in the French papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress is to push down or lower.

explanation.surface: A battle with a magnetic attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A field is a battlefield and also a region of force, as in a magnetic field.

clue.text: More, many more, indicate an accumulation in the 21

parts.note: more means extra
to point is to indicate
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
over means more, as in over a figure

explanation.surface: Ever more piling up out on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra, cover and point are each cricket fielding positions, so the full name piles them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra cover point is a cricket fielding position whose name stacks three other positions.

parts.note: a chump is a fool
to get the chop is to be sacked

explanation.surface: A fool is dismissed along with the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chump chop is a cut of lamb or mutton from the chump end of the loin.

clue.text: Recovery of tree with viral disease

indicators.note: disease upsets the letters, which come out disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree recovers after a viral disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrieval is getting something back, which is what recovery means.

clue.text: Confession of being 20-ed left out by soak

indicators.note: the letter for left is put out of the phrase

parts.note: 20 down is depress; someone depressed confesses I'm blue

explanation.surface: A drunk confesses to being depressed and left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confession of being 20-ed' means saying you are depressed: I'M BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to soak or saturate, as with dye or a feeling.

clue.text: Duelling Dickensian doctor goes to prison

definitions.meaning: Doctor ... challenges Mr Winkle to a duel in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A doctor from Dickens who fights a duel ends up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Slammer is the Pickwick Papers duellist, and the slammer is slang for jail.

definitions.meaning: a totter is British slang for a rag-and-bone man who collects scrap

explanation.surface: Dancers do reels while collecting scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Totters sway unsteadily, and totters are also scrap collectors in British slang.
